title: Quarterly Commitment Mosaic: Hosted API Catalog Sprints & Overflow Strategy
text:
Quarterly Commitment Mosaic: Hosted API Catalog Sprints & Overflow Strategy

description:
Define a repeatable quarterly planning artifact that allocates committed sprints for Hosted API + model catalog core work while preserving an overflow lane for emergent model onboarding, capacity hedging, and urgent reliability fixes. Deliverables: commitment mosaic document, sprint allocation guidelines, canary windows schedule, and a lightweight playbook for moving items between committed and overflow lanes.

problem_statement:
Current quarterly plans are rigidly prescriptive and flood PM/ENG during model surge windows. This causes either missed onboarding opportunities (blocking customers) or reactive re-prioritization that increases cross-team friction and runway risk. We need a planning construct that balances a stable committed backlog with a pre-authorized overflow lane and clear decision criteria for movement.

goals:
Provide a visual planning artifact (mosaic) that maps committed sprint lanes vs overflow lanes for the quarter
Reduce ad-hoc roadmap churn by 50% through defined movement criteria and pre-approved overflow capacity
Improve hosted-api model onboarding lead time from request to canary from 21 days to <=10 days for high-priority models
Ensure at least 95% of committed items complete within the quarter or receive formal roll-forward notes

success_metrics:
Quarterly committed completion rate >= 95%
Mean time from model onboarding request to canary <= 10 days for priority-1
Number of emergency re-prioritizations reduced by 50% vs previous quarter
Canary pass rate >= 98% for models onboarded through overflow lane

milestones:
2025-02-12: Kickoff and cross-functional alignment (PM/ENG/Design/Infra)
2025-02-26: Draft commitment mosaic and overflow rules published to Confluence
2025-03-11: Review with runtime/ops leads and finalize capacity hedging thresholds
2025-03-18: Canary windows schedule approved and calendarized
2025-03-25: Playbook and runbook merged into docs; stakeholder training session
2025-04-30: End-of-quarter retrospective and metrics review

rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (weeks 1-2): Create mosaic and decision rubric; get leadership sign-off
Phase 2 (weeks 3-5): Pilot overflow lane with two model onboarding requests and one reliability fix
Phase 3 (weeks 6-8): Expand to cross-org adoption; integrate overflow signals into Console alerts
Phase 4 (week 9): Post-mortem and iterate rules for next quarter

risks:
Ambiguity in movement criteria leads to silent scope creep
Overflow lane gets overloaded and starves committed work
Capacity hedges are insufficient during an unexpected model surge
Siloed decision-making causing downstream deploy or SLA regressions

mitigation:
Define explicit entry/exit criteria for overflow queue (severity, customer, capacity cost)
Reserve a hard ceiling of 12% of total sprint capacity for overflow by default
Require 'overflow approval' from runtime + infra leads for any item exceeding 8% capacity
Instrument dashboard: overflow queue length, mean time in queue, canary success rate

notes:
Design pattern inspired by 'swimlane with buffer' from platform planning experiments Q3 2024
This artifact should live under Confluence: /HostedAPI/Quarterly-Mosaics
We will use the existing roadmap board in Linear with new labels 'mosaic-committed' and 'mosaic-overflow'
Consider a follow-up initiative to automate overflow gating via Console feature flags

updates:
2025-02-12: Kickoff completed. Agreed to pilot mosaic approach this quarter. Action: Marco to draft decision rubric.
2025-02-19: Draft rubric posted. Feedback from Leah: clarify KB cache vs kernel-selection impacts for capacity calc.
2025-02-24: Decision: reserve 12% sprint capacity for overflow; approved by Eng leads. Action: ENG to add capacity tracker to dashboards (ENG-4821).
2025-03-04: Pilot model onboarding request #1 accepted into overflow lane after infra sign-off; canary scheduled 2025-03-15.
2025-03-11: Runtime team flagged potential risk if overflow-items with long seq-lengths exceed budget. Mitigation: temporary seq-length throttle for overflow canaries.
2025-03-18: Canary pass succeeded for model #1. Marco: recommend tightening approval for high-cost quantization work. Preparing playbook updates.
